overall: Los Angeles has already passed its daily peak, with the observed maximum of 77.0°F recorded around 17:25 ET (roughly 14:25 PT), and temperatures have since cooled to 73.4°F with a negative 2-hour velocity of -0.9°F/hr. The day ran hotter than the NWP model consensus (GFS=76.4, ECMWF=73.5, HRRR=75.6, NBM=73.5) but well below the NWS text forecast high of 81°F, reflecting a moderate marine influence with patchy fog and south winds keeping a lid on extreme heating.
forecast_obs_alerts_notes: All four NWP models undershot the observed running max of 77.0°F, with ECMWF and NBM at 73.5°F being furthest off and GFS closest at 76.4°F. The Beach Hazards Statement from NWS LA/Oxnard (dangerous rip currents, elevated surf through July 16) is consistent with an active south-to-southwest onshore flow regime that both moderated afternoon heating and caused models to underestimate the actual peak.
max_temp_prediction: With the peak now 4+ hours in the past, temperatures cooling steadily, and no mechanism for a nocturnal rebound, the TMAX for today is effectively locked in at 77.0°F. The INTRADAY model strongly confirms this with an 83% probability on the 76-77F even bucket — far outweighing the D1_NOW model's 56% on 74-75F, which is anchored to NWP forecasts that observations have already surpassed. Confidence is very high that TMAX lands in the 76-77F even bucket.
